lines: Chaos operators: adds memory, morph, cruise and freeze controls to a Sapphire chaos module, and goes immediately to the left of Frolic, Glee, Lark or Zoo
Selects one of 16 memory cells, numbered 0 to 15, for the store and recall controls; the chosen address appears on the display
Attenuates and inverts the memory select CV; turned fully clockwise, each half volt of that CV moves the address by one cell
Stores the current state of the chaos module to the right in the selected memory cell
Restores the chaos module to the right to the state held in the selected memory cell
Toggles whether simulated time in the chaos module to the right advances; the morph mix keeps taking effect while time is stopped
Mixes what the chaos module puts out between position vectors at 0 and velocity vectors at 1, with a weighted blend in between
Attenuates and inverts the morph CV
Regulates the speed of the chaotic particle, from its own widely varying speed at 0 to a nearly constant speed at 1
Attenuates and inverts the cruise CV
Switches the freeze input between gate and trigger; yellow for gate, dark for trigger
Moves the selected memory address; addresses wrap, so going past 15 arrives at 0 and going below 0 arrives at 15
A trigger here stores the chaos module's state in the selected memory cell
A trigger here restores the chaos module's state from the selected memory cell
In gate mode this input and the F button combine by exclusive-or to set whether simulated time is stopped; in trigger mode each pulse toggles that state
Moves the mix between position and velocity output
Moves the amount of speed regulation applied to the chaotic particle
Note — this expander has no effect by itself: place it immediately to the left of Frolic, Glee, Lark or Zoo, and its controls then act on that module.
Menu — Low sensitivity — on an attenuverter knob's own menu, not the panel menu: divides that knob's effect by 10 and marks the knob with an orange dot
Menu — Unipolar mode — on an attenuverter knob's own menu, not the panel menu: adds 5V to the CV on that control and clamps the result at zero
Multi-tap stereo and polyphonic delay, carrying one delay tap of its own along with the feedback, freeze, clear, clock and input gain shared by every tap in the chain
Adds an Echo Tap to the right, cloned from this tap's settings, shifting the rest of the chain over to make room
Sets the delay time of this tap, from 0.1 seconds to 10 seconds; right-clicking it chooses whether this tap runs free or follows the clock
Attenuates and inverts the delay time CV
Sets how much delayed audio is fed back: in serial mode from the last tap into the first, in parallel mode within each tap on its own
Attenuates and inverts the feedback CV
Places this tap in the stereo field; panning happens after the feedback path, so it moves where this tap lands without changing what flows to the next tap
Attenuates and inverts the panning CV
Sets the volume of this tap, outside the feedback path, so it changes the tap's loudness without changing the audio flowing through the chain
Attenuates and inverts the level CV
Reverses playback of this tap; with a gate patched to the reverse input, pressing it inverts the sense of that gate. Clicking the REV label switches to FLP, which reverses inside the feedback path
Stops new audio being written into every tap's buffer while keeping what is already recorded; with a gate patched to the freeze input, pressing it inverts the sense of that gate
Empties the delay buffers of every tap in the chain at once
Turns clock sync on or off for every tap in the chain at once
Snaps clock-synced delay times to musical divisions such as eighth notes, dotted eighths and triplets
Turns on a period of silence followed by a ramp in recording level after each clear or reset, in place of recording at once; both times are set by menu sliders
Switches the send and final output ports between stereo and polyphonic; in polyphonic mode the left ports carry every channel and the right ports carry one channel of 0V
Sets the level of audio entering Echo, from silence to a factor of 8, about +18dB, with 0dB leaving the input unchanged
Attenuates and inverts the input gain CV
Places the send and return before the delay, so processed audio flows on through the chain, or after it, so processed audio stays local to this tap
Silences this tap
Silences every tap in the chain except this one
Sets the gain of this tap's envelope follower output
Resets every Echo, Echo Tap and Echo Out in the chain to default settings
Resets this tap to its default settings, leaving the other taps alone
Left audio into the delay; with the right input empty this one feeds both sides, and a cable of 1 to 16 channels here sets the channel count of the whole chain
Right audio into the delay
Scaled a volt per octave: each positive volt halves this tap's delay time and each negative volt doubles it
Varies the amount of feedback around the chain
Moves this tap's position in the stereo field
Varies the level of audio entering Echo
Varies the volume of this tap
Left audio returning into this tap; patching this port breaks the internal short from the send ports on both the left and the right side
Right audio returning into this tap
In gate mode a high level reverses this tap; in trigger mode each pulse toggles it. The symbol above the REV label is clicked to change between the two modes
In gate mode a high level freezes every buffer in the chain; in trigger mode each pulse toggles the freeze. Its channels are summed to one value applied across the whole chain
A trigger here empties every tap's delay buffer; its channels are summed to one value applied across the whole chain
Sets the base delay time from the interval between rising edges, read high above 1V and low below 0.1V, and each tap's TIME multiplies that base. Clicking the CLOCK label switches to RATE
Left audio leaving this tap for outboard processing; it carries valid audio whether or not the return ports are patched
Right audio leaving this tap for outboard processing
Follows the amplitude of this tap, clamped to 0-10V through a bicubic limiter. Clicking the ENV label switches to DCK, where the voltage is 10V minus the envelope
Note — in RATE mode the clock port is read a volt per octave with 0V meaning 1Hz, and the delay time stays clamped to 0.1 seconds to 10 seconds, about 3.322 volts either side of 0V
Menu — DC reject cutoff — sets the frequency of the high-pass filter that strips DC from the input, 20Hz to 400Hz
Menu — Interpolator — chooses Linear (uses less CPU) or Sinc (cleaner audio) for reading the delay lines
Menu — Polyphonic envelope output — switches this tap's envelope follower between one channel and one per audio channel; it is on the panel menu and on the envelope output port's own menu
Note — the chain's audio output is on Echo Out, at the right-hand end; one is added there automatically when Echo is taken from the module browser, and without it the delay has no way out.
Menu — Initialize Echo expander chain — returns every Echo, Echo Tap and Echo Out in the chain to default settings
Menu — Signal routing — chooses Parallel, where every tap receives the input and plays back on its own, or Serial, where each tap feeds the next and the last feeds back into the first
Menu — Post-reset silence time — sets how long the taps record nothing after a clear or a reset, 0.1 seconds to 10 seconds, when the fader button is on
Menu — Post-reset ramp time — sets how long the recording level takes to rise from zero after that silence, 0.1 seconds to 10 seconds
Menu — Toggle all clock sync — turns clock sync on or off for every tap in the chain at once
Menu — Toggle polyphonic/mono on all envelope followers — switches every tap's envelope follower between one channel and one per audio channel
Menu — Tape speed slew rate — sets how quickly a tap's playback speed may change when its delay time moves, which trades pitch swoops against a lagging response
Menu — Freeze input port mode — chooses Gate or Trigger for the freeze input; it is on the panel menu and on the freeze input port's own menu
Menu — Reverse/flip input port mode — chooses Gate or Trigger for the reverse input; it is on the panel menu and on the reverse input port's own menu
Menu — Time mode — chooses Seconds or Clock sync for this tap, and is on the TIME knob's own menu rather than the panel menu
Menu — Toggle sensitivity on all attenuverters — divides the effect of every attenuverter on the panel by 10, or restores them all
Menu — Low sensitivity — on an attenuverter knob's own menu, not the panel menu: divides that knob's effect by 10 and marks the knob with an orange dot
Menu — Unipolar mode — on an attenuverter knob's own menu, not the panel menu: adds 5V to the CV on that control and clamps the result at zero
Echo.notes: The two gate-or-trigger port modes are named in the source as "Reverse/flip input port mode" and "Freeze input port mode", built from the toggle group's menuName plus " input port mode"; both appear on the panel menu and on their own input port's menu.

lines: Mixes a Sapphire Echo chain down to its stereo or polyphonic output, and goes to the right of the last Echo Tap
Balances dry against processed audio, fully dry counter-clockwise and fully processed clockwise
Attenuates and inverts the mix CV
Sets the overall output volume of the chain, dry and processed together
Attenuates and inverts the output level CV
Moves the balance between dry and processed audio
Varies the overall output volume of the chain
Left audio out of the whole chain; in polyphonic mode this port carries every channel
Right audio out of the whole chain; in polyphonic mode it carries one channel of 0V
Note — this expander has no effect by itself: place it to the right of the last Echo Tap, or of Echo, and the whole chain then comes out of its ports.
Note — deleting this module leaves the chain with no output; pressing the add-tap button on the last tap of a chain that has no Echo Out inserts one.
Menu — Low sensitivity — on an attenuverter knob's own menu, not the panel menu: divides that knob's effect by 10 and marks the knob with an orange dot
Menu — Unipolar mode — on an attenuverter knob's own menu, not the panel menu: adds 5V to the CV on that control and clamps the result at zero
Stereo synthesis filter that runs audio through a simulated hexagonal mesh of balls and springs, turning it into metallic, bell-like or drone textures, and able to self-oscillate with no input
Sets the friction that damps vibration in the mesh; higher settings cut the ringing short and lower settings let it run on like reverb
Sets the stiffness of the springs, the force per unit of stretch; higher stiffness generally raises the pitch of the sound
Sets the rest length of the springs; shorter than the ball spacing gives a bell-like quality, longer loosens the mesh into chaotic vibration
Sets an ambient magnetic field that bends the moving balls into circular paths: positive values align the field across the mesh, negative values through it, and zero turns it off
Scales the mass of the two impurity balls from 0.1 to 10 against the 20 balls of fixed mass, with 1 at centre making them the same
Attenuates and inverts the friction CV
Attenuates and inverts the stiffness CV
Attenuates and inverts the spring span CV
Attenuates and inverts the magnetic field CV
Attenuates and inverts the impurity mass CV
Sets how hard the input audio drives the input balls, which changes the shape the mesh is distorted into as well as the loudness
Sets the volume of the stereo output
Sets the direction in which the input balls are vibrated, 0 degrees perpendicular to the plane of the mesh and 90 degrees parallel to it, with 45 degrees the default
Sets the direction of ball movement the output is taken from, 0 degrees perpendicular to the plane of the mesh and 90 degrees parallel to it, with 45 degrees the default
Turns the simulation on and off; off drops CPU use to almost nothing, returns every ball to its starting position and fades the output over 2.5ms
Attenuates and inverts the input tilt CV
Attenuates and inverts the output tilt CV
Splits one polyphonic input cable into left and right, taking channel 1 as left and channel 2 as right, when only one audio input is patched
Sends both output channels to the left output as a 2-channel polyphonic signal, channel 1 left and channel 2 right
Varies the friction in the mesh
Varies the spring stiffness
Varies the spring rest length
Varies the strength and axis of the magnetic field
Varies the mass of the two impurity balls
Left audio into the mesh; its channels are summed to one voltage
Right audio into the mesh; its channels are summed to one voltage
Overrides the power button: the simulation runs above 1V and stops below 0.1V, holding its state between those levels, and polyphonic channels are summed first so several gates act as one logic gate
Varies the direction the input balls are vibrated in
Varies the direction the output is taken from
Left audio out of the mesh, one channel, taken from the movement of the left output ball
Right audio out of the mesh, one channel, taken from the movement of the right output ball
Menu — DC reject cutoff — sets the high-pass corner on both outputs anywhere from 20Hz to 400Hz, with 20Hz the default, which doubles as a way to thin out a muddy bass
Menu — Output limiter — sets an automatic gain control threshold from 1V to 10V, 4V by default, or turns it off at the far right; the OUT knob glows red while it is reducing gain
Menu — Model sample rate — runs the physics at Match engine rate or at a fixed 22050, 24000, 32000, 44100, 48000, 88200 or 96000 Hz, which fixes the sound against engine settings
Menu — Send right output as vector to Tricorder — chooses which output ball's 3D position goes to a Tricorder on the right
Menu — Limiter warning light — turns off the red glow on the OUT knob without turning the limiter off
Menu — Toggle sensitivity on all attenuverters — divides the effect of every attenuverter on the panel by 10, or restores them all
Menu — Enable input stereo splitter — does what the button between the input ports does, taking channel 1 of a polyphonic cable in the left input as left and channel 2 as right
Menu — Send polyphonic stereo to L output — does what the button between the output ports does, sending both channels to the left output as one 2-channel signal
Menu — Low sensitivity — on an attenuverter knob's own menu, not the panel menu: divides that knob's effect by 10 and marks the knob with an orange dot
Menu — Unipolar mode — on an attenuverter knob's own menu, not the panel menu: adds 5V to the CV on that control and clamps the result at zero
Note — the mesh starts at rest and makes no sound by itself: patch audio into the input ports, or find a control setting where the mesh self-oscillates.
Elastika.notes: ElastikaEngine::initialize calls mesh.Quiet(), so a fresh Elastika is silent; the maker's Elastika.md documents self-oscillation as something particular control settings produce, not the default.

lines: Input stage of an expandable chain of bandpass, notch and comb filters, carrying the audio inputs, the cascade control and a chaotic modulation source routed through the whole chain
Adds an Empath Filter to the right, cloned from the settings of the filter used to add it, shifting the rest of the chain over to make room
Switches the chain between stereo and polyphonic; in polyphonic mode the left input feeds every channel and the right output and send ports carry one channel of 0V
Sets how many filter stages, 1 to 3, each filter expander in the chain runs in series, which steepens the slope and narrows the response
Attenuates and inverts the cascade CV
Sets the rate of the built-in chaotic modulation source that is routed to every control in the chain
Attenuates and inverts the chaos speed CV, and with nothing patched there it sets how much internal chaos modulates the chaos speed itself
Sets the overall depth of the chaotic modulation reaching the whole chain; at zero no chaos reaches any control
Attenuates and inverts the chaos level CV
Resets every Empath, Empath Filter and Empath Out in the chain to default settings
Switches the spectrum graph on each filter between one trace and one trace per channel
Gives the left and right channels separate chaotic modulation when on, or one shared chaotic signal when off; with more than two channels it alternates the two signals across odd and even channels
Randomizes the chaotic modulation source across the whole chain at once
Sets the level of audio entering the chain
Attenuates and inverts the input gain CV
Stops the chaotic modulation source, holding every chaotic voltage where it is, which also cuts CPU use
Shows the chaos voltages on the spectrum displays
Left audio into the chain; with the right input empty this one feeds both sides, and in polyphonic mode it carries every channel
Right audio into the chain
Varies the number of filter stages run in series by each filter in the chain
Varies the rate of the chaotic modulation source, and patching a cable here replaces the internal chaos on that control
Varies the depth of the chaotic modulation reaching the chain
Varies the level of audio entering the chain
Note — every control with an attenuverter is modulated by the internal chaos source through that attenuverter, and patching a cable into its CV input replaces the chaos with the cable's voltage

Note — this module has no output ports: the chain needs at least one Empath Filter and an Empath Output to its right, both added automatically when Empath is taken from the module browser.

lines: Polyphonic envelope follower and pitch detector, measuring the loudness and the pitch of a single tone in the incoming audio by counting samples between zero crossings

Attenuates and inverts the threshold CV
Sets how fast the reported pitch is slewed; slow settings glide between notes but hold steady, fast settings jump to new notes and waver more
Attenuates and inverts the speed CV

Attenuates and inverts the centre frequency CV

Takes the vector a Tricorder is graphing out to ports, and goes immediately to the right of it

The z component of the received vector, scaled by LEVEL
A copy of the trigger that asked the Tricorder on the left to clear its display
The received vector as a 3-channel polyphonic signal, x on channel 1, y on channel 2 and z on channel 3
Note — the level-adjusted vector is also passed on to any module immediately to the right, so several of these can be chained
Note — this module has no ports of its own to feed: place it immediately to the right of a Tricorder, and the vector that Tricorder is graphing comes out of its ports.

Note — hovering over the display brings up its controls: chevrons at each edge spin the plot, XYZ shows or hides the axes, 123 shows or hides the voltages as numbers, plus and minus zoom

lines: Stereo waveguide synthesizer: air driven into a chamber vibrates a spring-loaded piston, and pressure waves travelling down a resonant tube become the stereo output
Sets the rate at which air is forced into the chamber, which is how hard the instrument is blown
Sets how quickly vibrations reflecting back and forth in the tube die out; larger values reverberate longer
Sets the rotation applied to the stereo polarization of pressure reflected from the far end of the tube
Sets the strength of the piston spring; a stiffer spring vibrates faster
Sets the diameter of the valve the air escapes through; narrow settings turn small piston movements into large changes of escape rate and sound shriller, wide settings sound more mellow
Sets the height of the escape valve against the piston's travel; higher settings need more chamber pressure before air escapes into the tube
Sets the resonant frequency of the tube by making it longer or shorter, marked in Hz; it is not a volt per octave control
Sets the angular rotation given to the polarization of air entering the tube
Attenuates and inverts the airflow CV
Attenuates and inverts the decay CV
Attenuates and inverts the angle CV
Attenuates and inverts the spring CV
Attenuates and inverts the width CV
Attenuates and inverts the centre CV
Attenuates and inverts the root frequency CV
Attenuates and inverts the vortex CV
Sets the volume of the stereo output; it glows red while the output limiter is reducing gain
Varies the rate air is forced into the chamber
Varies how quickly reflections in the tube die out
Varies the stereo rotation applied to reflected pressure
Varies the stiffness of the piston spring
Varies the diameter of the escape valve
Varies the height of the escape valve against the piston's travel
Varies the resonant frequency of the tube
Varies the rotation given to air entering the tube

In VENT mode a level above 1V opens the chamber, letting the air out and cutting off the audio inputs, and it closes again below 0.1V. Clicking the word VENT switches to SEAL, which inverts that logic
Left audio injected into the resonant tube, where it mixes with the pressure from the piston; only DECAY, ANGLE and ROOT act on it, and those control groups light up while a cable is patched
Right audio injected into the resonant tube, where it mixes with the pressure from the piston; only DECAY, ANGLE and ROOT act on it, and those control groups light up while a cable is patched
Left audio out, the real part of the complex tube pressure
Right audio out, the imaginary part of the complex tube pressure
Note — all eleven input ports set the polyphony: the one with the most channels sets the channel count of both outputs, and an input with fewer channels repeats its last channel across the rest
Menu — Output limiter — sets an automatic gain control threshold from 1V to 10V, 4V by default, or turns it off at the far right; the OUT knob glows red while it is reducing gain
Menu — Toggle VENT/SEAL — inverts the sense of the vent input, doing by menu what clicking the VENT label does
Menu — Limiter warning light — turns off the red glow on the OUT knob without turning the limiter off
Menu — Toggle sensitivity on all attenuverters — divides the effect of every attenuverter on the panel by 10, or restores them all
Menu — Low sensitivity — on an attenuverter knob's own menu, not the panel menu: divides that knob's effect by 10 and marks the knob with an orange dot
Menu — Unipolar mode — on an attenuverter knob's own menu, not the panel menu: adds 5V to the CV on that control and clamps the result at zero
